messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: decode-gpu-oom on pool us-east-1-decode-3 — elevated error rate and request drops detected. auto-pager sent to oncall.
maria_oncall: Got it. I'm onpager. Key symptoms?
jon_sre: Seeing repeated CUDA OOM at decode step, containers restarting on node us-east-1-decode-3a. Logs: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.3 GiB` then kube restart loop. Request drops ~18% for streaming route.
maria_oncall: Is this correlated with a customer spike? Any header anomalies?
ashley_runtime: Telemetry shows a small set of requests with huge requested max_tokens — looks like a client misconfigured `max_tokens: 20000` in streaming mode. KV cache growth + long decode = OOM. Stack traces point at decode-loop growth and no early token cap.
leo_support: We're already getting a customer ticket (ID 45678) with complaint about truncated/chat errors. I'll flag them as impacted.
maria_oncall: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) Apply token cap at router to reject >2048; 2) Route new streaming traffic off the affected pool to fallback smaller model; 3) Throttle concurrent streams from offending API key. Which is quickest?
jon_sre: Fastest is a router rule to reject big max_tokens and an emergency route change. I can push a temporary route policy. Use this curl to add cap: `curl -X POST https://router.internal/rules -d '{"match":"route==/v1/stream","max_tokens":2048,"reason":"emergency token cap"}'`
maria_oncall: Jon please apply the rule and confirm. Ashley, can you prepare a smaller compatible model for fallback (quantized)?
ashley_runtime: I can serve a 7B quantized variant as fallback in ~10m. Will also enable prefix KV eviction to reduce memory per session.
jon_sre: Rule pushed, repo response: `201 Created` — router is rejecting >2048 with 429 now. Pushing traffic away from us-east-1-decode-3 to pool us-east-1-decode-1/2 as a backup.
maria_oncall: Great. Monitor OOM counts and request drop rate.
jon_sre: OOM spikes dropping from ~45/min to ~3/min after routing change. Restart loops still occurring on the 3a node; I've cordoned it: `kubectl cordon us-east-1-decode-3a`.
ashley_runtime: Fallback model warmed and accepting traffic. I've enabled `kv_prefix_eviction: true` on the runtime agents and lowered per-request kv retention to 2 sequences.
leo_support: Notifying customer via ticket 45678: "We've applied temporary safeguards and routed your traffic to a fallback model; investigating root cause — we'll follow up."
maria_oncall: Any container crashes beyond the one node?
jon_sre: Isolated to that node. Kernel OOM messages show memory fragmentation + CUDA OOM. Raising an infra ticket to check GPU driver version drift.
ashley_runtime: We also observed some streaming sessions never sending `end_stream` and keeping KV alive — likely client side. Adding an enforcement: close idle streams > 60s.
maria_oncall: Nice. Can we add a short-term quota on concurrent streams per key?
jon_sre: Added `concurrent_stream_limit: 10` for keys with >100rps. Policy applied.
ashley_runtime: With router cap + fallback + eviction + concurrent limit, error rate down to baseline. Request drops dropped to <1%.
leo_support: Customer acknowledges mitigation, asks for ETA on full fix. I'll draft a status update.
maria_oncall: Next steps: - Run node repro to reproduce allocation pattern - Validate driver and CUDA runtime versions on affected node - Implement longer-term guard in runtime to enforce per-request token limit and early-kill runaway decodes - Postmortem and customer RCA.
jon_sre: I'll collect `dmesg`, container logs, and GPU driver logs and attach to incident.
ashley_runtime: Will add unit tests for max_tokens enforcement and handle streaming clients that don't send `end_stream`.
maria_oncall: Thanks all — I'll close pager once OOMs stop for 20m and ticket updated. :thumbsup:
customer-handoff-bot: Customer update sent for ticket 45678 by leo_support.
jon_sre: OOM counts stable at 0 for past 12m, no new restarts after cordon/evacuate.
maria_oncall: Closing pager in 5. Followups in postmortem channel.
